complete_package_official.package: v231 Linear (L-EM3 K=2) complete root + L-AD1, v195 Attention body unchanged
complete_package_official.note: Exact seconds and score unknown; no prediction is written. Parent v231 official reading was 291s against the 300s limit (9s of headroom).

decision: REJECTED. The root is unchanged at v231 (18518/291s) and the fallback root is unchanged at v233 (18428/288s). The implementation is closed: no step/window/candidate-count retry, and it is not transplanted into any other candidate.
why_this_timeout_is_recorded_differently: v232 was locally time-neutral, so its timeout could be read as 'there was no measurable gain to show'. v235 is not that case: it is the only Linear candidate this round whose speed-up was resolvable locally (has-Gram calls at 34-52x the byte-identical sham null, consistent in direction across 24-30 of 31 rounds, +4.26%/+4.63% on calls costing 548/894 ms), which folds to roughly 8-13 s over 336 calls -- the same order as the 4 s v233 actually collected officially. It still timed out. The reading this supports is the pre-existing rule, not a new one: a locally resolvable speed-up is not a guarantee of an official pass.
no_variance_inference: The official channel returned only 'timeout'. Nothing was reported about by how much, so no inference is drawn about the official clock's variance or spread, and no conversion factor between local and official seconds is derived from this single outcome.
projection_note: no projection was recorded, and none is warranted. The card's own acceptance condition (plan section 4.3) is a resolvable drop in the OFFICIAL seconds, not a local one, and this machine's wall clock cannot be converted into the official machine's. The 8-13 s figure above is quoted only as the card's own local expectation that did not materialize; it is not a prediction of any future candidate.
note: The official baseline for this reading is the v231 root at 18518 / 291s against a 300s hard limit. v235 is a descendant of that root and carries the L-EM3 K=2 arm, so this reading is against v231 and is not additive with the v233 (L-TF1) fallback-root reading, which was priced against v230 at K=1. Every output field was bit-identical to the parent (336/336 paired cases exactly zero), so the score was never at stake; only the second was, and it did not fall inside the limit.
